newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-L&G Australia sales up 44.4 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-L&G Australia sales up 44.4 pct in 96.

text.p: Legal and General Group Plc's Australian unit said on Thursday its total new business in calendar 1996 rose 44.4 percent to A$615.3 million.

The company said that in line with recent industry trends, the growth was achieved in single premium business, up 51.8 percent to A$555.2 million, while new regular premium business was little changed from the previous year, down 0.4 percent to A$60.1 million.

Legal and General Australia managing director Derek Bullen said significant increases in annuities, group superannuation single premiums and infrastructure bonds were the highlights of the increased result.
He said the demand for infrastructure bonds had made the bonds the company's largest selling individual product of the year, worth A$161.5 million.

The company had mixed results in superannuation (pension) product sales. It increased group supperannuation single premium, up 28.3 percent to A$104.2 million, while small scheme single premium dropped by 8.5 percent to A$6.8 million.

Legal and General's overall single premium result was boosted by the inclusion of a full year's contribution from SGIC Life, which Legal and General acquired from the South Australian Government in 1995.
Excluding SGIC, single premiums rose by 38.4 percent to A$501.5 million.
